1. Fact: Bob is white.  
2. Rule: White people are blue → Bob is blue.  
3. Rule: If Bob is white and Bob is blue then Bob is round → Bob is round.  

Since we can derive that Bob is round, the statement “Bob is not round” contradicts this derivation.

ANSWER: False

- Bob is white. (Fact)
- Harry is green. (Fact)
- Round people are white. (Rule: If someone is round then they are white.)

- If Bob is white and Bob is blue then Bob is round. (Rule)
- Round, white people are not quiet. (Rule: If someone is round and white,str then they are not quiet.)
- If someone is blue and not white then they are smart. (Rule)
- If someone is white then they are not smart. (Rule)
- If someone is smart and not quiet then they are green. (Rule)
- All smart, round people are not green. (Rule: If someone is smart and round then not green.)

Goal: Determine if Bob is not round is entailed.

We might try to derive that Bob is round via rule: If Bob is white and Bob is blue then Bob is round. We have Bob is white. Also from rule: White people are blue => Bob is blue. So Bob is white AND blue => Bob is round. So we can deduce Bob is round.

Thus Bob is round. Therefore Bob is not round is false. However might there be contradictions? Also we have rule: If someone is white then they are not smart. So Bob is white => Bob not smart. That matches fact Bob not smart. Also rule: all smart & round => not green. But HDMI.

We also have rule: Round, white people are not quiet. So Bob round & white => not quiet. Then rule: If someone is smart and not quiet then they are green. But Bob not smart, so doesn't apply. Also rule: If someone is smart and round then not green. Bob not smart, so not apply.

But we can also derive that Bob is not quiet, but that doesn't affect roundness.

No rule to say not round. So Bob is round, thus Bob not round is false. Determine entailment: The statement "Bob is not round" is contradicted by derivation of Bob round. So answer: False.

But we must be careful: Are there any rules that could produce not round? There's rule: Round, white people are not quiet. Not relevant.

But we have rule: If someone is smart and not quiet then they are green. But if Bob were round, we would have Sutton: Bob not quiet. If Bob were smart, then green. But Bob not smart. So no.

Also rule: If someone is blue and not white then they are smart. Not apply.

Also rule: If someone is smart and not quiet then green. Not apply.

Also rule: All smart, round people are not green. Not apply.

No rule that yields not round.

Thus we can derive Bob round; thus Bob not round is false. So answer: False.
